course.title: MongoDB — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first 261-lesson MongoDB course built from the supplied 25-module curriculum: BSON, CRUD, MQL, aggregation, data modeling, indexes, validation, transactions, drivers, specialized features, distributed systems, security, operations, migrations and production readiness.
course.version_scope: Official MongoDB documentation and driver references checked 2026-10-15. Most core examples use mongosh syntax. Confirm exact feature support against the installed server and driver versions and the selected self-managed or Atlas deployment. Atlas Search, Vector Search, Atlas automation/monitoring and certain advanced operations are marked as deployment-dependent or optional.
audience: beginners and students learning document databases
backend developers using Node.js or Python
database engineers moving into MongoDB operations
developers exploring search, events and distributed database concepts
prerequisites: Introductory JSON and nested object concepts.
JavaScript or Python is helpful for driver modules.
Basic database concepts are helpful but not required.
course.estimated_workload_hours: 85–120 hours; pace depends on how much of the optional specialist and distributed-operations material is completed in a real lab.
learning_outcomes: Explain documents, collections, BSON and MongoDB architecture.
Set up a local or managed practice environment and use mongosh/Compass safely.
Perform CRUD and compose MQL filters and update operations.
Build aggregation pipelines and design document models around application access patterns.
Choose indexes, validate document shapes and reason about atomicity and transactions.
Integrate official Node.js and Python drivers into backend code.
Recognize specialized features including time-series, geospatial, GridFS, Search, Vector Search and change streams.
Evaluate replication/sharding concepts, apply security practices, and plan backup, recovery, migration, testing and production readiness.

learning_roadmap.title: Foundations
learning_roadmap.milestone: Understand document databases, BSON, setup, Compass and mongosh.

learning_roadmap.title: Core queries and writes
learning_roadmap.milestone: Practice CRUD, MQL filters, array queries, update operators and bulk operations.

learning_roadmap.title: Analysis and data modeling
learning_roadmap.milestone: Build aggregation reports and choose intentional document relationships.

learning_roadmap.title: Correctness and performance
learning_roadmap.milestone: Add indexes, validation and transaction/retry reasoning.

learning_roadmap.title: Application integration
learning_roadmap.milestone: Use official drivers and recognize when specialized collection features fit.

learning_roadmap.title: Optional search and event processing
learning_roadmap.milestone: Explore search, vector retrieval and change streams as optional branches.

learning_roadmap.title: Distributed systems
learning_roadmap.milestone: Understand replica sets, failover, sharding and scale limitations.

learning_roadmap.title: Security and operations
learning_roadmap.milestone: Harden access, monitor workloads and rehearse backup/recovery.

learning_roadmap.title: Professional delivery
learning_roadmap.milestone: Deliver migrations, quality checks, deployment plans and production-readiness evidence.

curriculum_notes.core_modules: Modules 1–14 and 20–25; individual advanced lessons in these modules still require the deployment-appropriate lab/review.
curriculum_notes.advanced_modules: Modules 7–15 and 17–25 include intermediate-to-professional topics such as bulk operations, aggregation, schema design, transactions, drivers, replication, sharding and operations.
curriculum_notes.optional_specialist_modules: Modules 15–17 cover specialized collections, Atlas Search/Vector Search and change streams. Search, vector and Atlas-specific controls are optional; they are not prerequisites for CRUD development.
curriculum_notes.execution_policy: Lesson examples use static-validation/reference output and are not executed by CodeLeaf in-page. Real shell/driver behavior requires a separate, isolated MongoDB runtime. Never execute arbitrary learner code inside FastAPI or the production container.
curriculum_notes.gamification_policy: No course-authored XP overrides. The existing platform backend remains authoritative for base XP, plan boosts, idempotency and certificates.
